title: Late Fees, Draw Holds and Service Entitlements of TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours
content:
TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours block sizes differ in their late-fee terms, in when draws are held for an unpaid invoice, and in the service entitlements that come with the size.

| Figure | 10-Hour | 20-Hour | 40-Hour | 80-Hour | 160-Hour | 320-Hour |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly late fee on an unpaid block invoice past the grace period (percent) | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 |
| Calendar days after the due date before a late fee is assessed | 5 | 5 | 5 | 10 | 10 | 10 |
| Minimum late fee per invoice per month (USD) | 25.00 | 25.00 | 25.00 | 35.00 | 50.00 | 50.00 |
| Days an invoice of a signature-activated block may be past due before draws are put on hold | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 30 | 30 |
| Hours statement emailed to the authorized contact | monthly | monthly | monthly | monthly | weekly | weekly |
| Block work scheduled ahead of uncommitted time-and-materials requests (priority scheduling) | no | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Named engineer assigned to block work | no | no | no | no | yes | yes |

## Notes

- Only the 160-Hour and 320-Hour Blocks are activated on signature, so the draw-hold figure has effect on those two sizes; the smaller sizes show 0.
- Priority scheduling and a named engineer are entitlements of the size and are not billed separately.
- Hypothetical illustration: an unpaid balance of 1000.00 at 1.5 percent gives 15.00, so the 25.00 minimum applies on a 40-Hour Block and the 50.00 minimum on a 160-Hour Block.
